runs.head: bfb4ac7653f6
runs.summary: Ran all six Done Contract checks (pass), diffed the vendored engine, pack, ruleset, workflow, template and AGENTS.md against the framework at the SOURCE commit (identical; settings rules match the seed; the framework's own 143 tests pass), and probed the guard by hand. Then exercised claim, save, the stop and pulse hooks, takeover and review in a scratch project with a local remote: the claim rules behave as described, but a review run that starts ten minutes after the ticket's last event leaves the branch diverged from the remote, and the new engine revives ticket 8.

findings.claim: `run` reads `head` before `keep_alive`, which commits and pushes a `saved` event when the ticket's last event is at least `save_minutes` old; after the reviewer, `git reset --hard head` moves the branch back behind that pushed commit. The review run is then committed on the old head and its push is refused as a non-fast-forward, so the run never reaches the remote and every later push of the branch is refused too (sequence: a ticket in `reviewing`, `rail advance` more than ten minutes after its last event, such as a session coming back from a pause or after an invalid-output review).
findings.check: A test that runs `rail advance` on a ticket in `reviewing` whose last event is older than `[claim] save_minutes`, and asserts that the local branch and the remote branch have the same tip afterwards.

evidence.command: Scratch clone with a bare remote, MEDIUM ticket 2 shipped, first review run invalid (state reviewing). Then `python3 later.py advance 2` (rail with minutes_since() answering 11 more) and `git rev-parse --short` / `git log --oneline -3` of the local and remote branch; then a plain `rail advance 2`.

runs.head: 35d40d342db7
runs.summary: Re-reviewed the whole change. All six Done Contract checks pass. `.rail/engine`, `.rail/packs`, `.rail/ruleset.json`, the workflow and the ticket template are byte-identical to the framework at the commit in `.rail/SOURCE`, and that commit's own 145 tests pass. `.claude/settings.json` has the seed's rules. F1 is fixed (the sign of life is written before the head is read) and F2 is fixed (`rail status` shows ticket 8 dropped, with a `rail drop 8` mark on `rail/ids`). About 40 guard probes found one remaining fail-open, reported below with one wording mismatch; neither blocks the merge.

findings.claim: A `cd` the guard can't follow is recognised only when `cd`, `pushd` or `popd` is the first word of a simple command. After `cd OTHER_REPO &&`, a `cd -` inside a brace group, after `then`, or after `!` is missed, so the push to `main` or `gh pr merge` that follows is judged as the other repository's and allowed. This is the sweep's F1 case in another spelling, and `docs/guards.md` says whatever can't be followed is judged as this project's.
findings.check: A guard test that expects deny for `cd OTHER && { cd -; git push origin main; }`, `cd OTHER && if true; then cd -; fi && git push origin main` and `cd OTHER && ! cd - && git push origin main`, where OTHER is another git repository.

evidence.command: Piped each command line to `RAIL_CLOUD=0 .rail/bin/rail hook guard` as a Bash PreToolUse event with cwd set to the ticket's worktree; /tmp/other is another git repository on branch main.

findings.claim: The ticket's Why says work a session abandoned is resumed after an hour, but the engine copied in resumes it after `[claim] stale_minutes` = 30 (config.py default, and the ticket's own Look at says 30 minutes). The Why becomes the pull request's description, so the owner is told twice the real limit.

findings.claim: The save hooks don't know a review is running: when the session's PostToolUse hook fires while its own `rail advance` is inside a review (a parallel tool call, or advance run in the background), `save_work` commits and pushes the reviewer's in-scope scratch files. The review's `git reset --hard head` then moves the branch back behind that push, so the `review` commit never reaches the remote and local and remote stay diverged (the same end state as F1).
findings.check: A test whose review command writes a file inside scope_paths and sleeps, runs `rail hook pulse` for the same session meanwhile, and asserts the remote branch has no scratch file and equals the local branch after advance.

runs.summary: Ran all six Done Contract checks (pass), confirmed the engine, pack, ruleset, workflow and settings match the framework at the commit in .rail/SOURCE, ran the framework's 151 tests against that identical engine (pass), replayed about 85 guard command lines including the spellings from F3, F7 and F8 (all now denied or asked as documented), and drove `rail save` and the hooks in scratch clones with a bare remote. findings.claim: `save_work` passes every dirty path to `git add -A -- <paths>`, which dies with `pathspec did not match any files` for a staged deletion. runs.head: f45d1c4a8f46
runs.summary: Security seat: ran ~80 command lines through `rail hook guard` and compared `guard.deny`/`guard.ask` against the engine on main, then built a scratch repository to exercise the new contract-merged approval path, and read the save, provision and machine-hook code. The Done Contract's guard cases hold, but the new code adds two authorization holes (one guard regression, one self-approval path) and an unchecked auto-push.

findings.claim: A ticket file on the base branch with no branch and no ship is now recorded as `accepted by person via merge`, with no check that a person merged a contract pull request. Ticket files are excluded from the scope check, so an auto-merged LOW ticket whose branch adds `.rail/tickets/99.md` (tier HIGH, scope `.rail/engine/**`) gets the HIGH contract approved and claimed by the next `rail next` with no person involved; the engine on main showed the same ticket as `dropped`.
findings.check: A test: commit a HIGH ticket file to the base branch under another ticket's `Ticket:` trailer, with no branch and no pull request, run `rail next`, and assert no `accepted` event with `by: person` is written.

evidence.command: scratch repo, no remote: commit .rail/tickets/99.md (tier HIGH, scope .rail/engine/**) on main under trailer 'Ticket: 1 / Tier: LOW'; RAIL_CLOUD=0 .rail/bin/rail next --json; git show 99-change-the-engine:.rail/journal/99-events.jsonl  (and `rail status` with main's engine on a copy)

findings.claim: `_gh_named` treats any `gh` argument containing `github.com/` as naming a repository, including the value of `--body` or `-f`, so a merge of this project's pull request passes when its message mentions another repository's URL: `gh pr merge 5 --body "see github.com/other/repo"`. The engine on main denied this command; with the new rule that a merged unshipped pull request counts as the person's approval, it also lets an agent approve its own contract.
findings.check: A guard test: `gh pr merge 5 --body "see github.com/other/repo"` and `gh api -X PUT repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/5/merge -f commit_message=https://github.com/other/repo/issues/1` must both return deny.

evidence.command: guard.deny(cmd,'main','9-x',cwd=worktree,locate=...,repo='timur-makarov/throw-away-repo') with main's engine and this change's engine; also printf ... | .rail/bin/rail hook guard

findings.claim: The new Stop and PostToolUse hooks commit and push every untracked file inside `scope_paths` with no check, and `.gitignore` lists only `.claude/worktrees/` and `__pycache__/`. A credential or dump file an agent writes into an in-scope folder (for example `calc/token.json` under scope `calc/**`) is pushed to GitHub at the end of the turn, before verify's secret scan ever runs.
findings.check: A test that `save_work` leaves out untracked files matching the guard's secret patterns (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`), or runs the project's secret scan before the push.

findings.claim: The merge deny matches only `gh pr merge` with the two words adjacent, and the guard doesn't read command substitutions or `case` arms, so `gh pr -R timur-makarov/throw-away-repo merge 5`, `echo $(git push origin HEAD:main)` in backticks or `$(...)`, `case x in x) git push -f origin x;; esac` and `cd /tmp && export GIT_DIR=<repo>/.git && git push origin main` all pass. These passed on main's engine too.
findings.check: Guard tests for each of these lines expecting deny.

runs.head: ceb59271a816
runs.summary: All six Done Contract checks pass, the vendored engine, pack and ruleset are byte-identical to the framework at the SOURCE commit (settings rules match the seed), and the framework's own 157 tests pass at that commit. I also probed the guard with about 40 command lines, re-derived this repository's tickets with the new engine, and simulated the new save hooks; F1 to F9 no longer reproduce, and one new advisory and one parked finding remain.

findings.claim: The PostToolUse throttle looks for its stamp under `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.git/rail/cache/pulse/`, but `rail hook pulse` writes it to the git common directory. In a session whose project directory is a git worktree (`.git` is a file there), the stamp is never found, so the pulse hook runs a fetch and a save after every tool call instead of at most every ten minutes, and commits and pushes in-scope changes each time.
findings.check: A test that runs the PostToolUse command from settings.json twice with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set to a linked worktree and asserts the second call is skipped.

evidence.command: In the ticket's worktree (`.git` is `gitdir: /home/user/throw-away-repo/.git/worktrees/9`), with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=$PWD and CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=probe-sess: ran the hook's own test `[ -n "$(find "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.git/rail/cache/pulse/${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-any}" -mmin -10 2>/dev/null)" ]` and, when it failed, `rail hook pulse`, twice in a row; then `ls /home/user/throw-away-repo/.git/rail/cache/pulse/`

findings.claim: The guard reads `GH_REPO` only as a prefix on the `gh` command itself, not when it is exported earlier in the line. So `cd OTHER_REPO && export GH_REPO=timur-makarov/throw-away-repo && gh pr merge 5` merges this project's pull request and is allowed; the engine on main allows it too, so this change did not cause it (an exported `GIT_DIR` is now followed, `GH_REPO` is not).
findings.check: A guard test case: after `cd OTHER &&`, `export GH_REPO=<this repo> && gh pr merge 5` must be denied.

runs.summary: Ran all six Done Contract checks (all pass), confirmed the vendored engine, pack, ruleset, workflow and ticket template are byte-identical to the framework at the commit in .rail/SOURCE, ran the framework's 158 tests against that engine (all pass), and probed the guard and the new claim, save and hold code with scratch scenarios. findings.claim: `quiet_minutes` counts every journal event as the claiming session's sign of life, including the `continued` event another session writes when it records a person's `rail:go`. runs.head: e2403f5acf5c
runs.summary: All six Done Contract checks pass, the vendored engine, pack, ruleset, workflow and settings rules are identical to the framework at the commit in .rail/SOURCE, and the framework's 161 tests pass on that engine; the earlier findings F1 to F16 no longer reproduce from the code and the tests that cover them. Probing the guard hook with about 80 command lines and reading the claim, save, hold and git-cache code turned up one new advisory problem: a false deny in the guard.

findings.claim: `deny` reuses the flag `aimed` (an exported GIT_DIR points later git commands at an unknown repository) for the result of `locate(there)` on a push target. After a push from another repository to a local folder that is a git repository, `aimed` is a non-empty tuple, so every later git command in the line is judged as this project's: `cd OTHER && git push /path/backup.git main && git push origin main` is denied, though both pushes are another repository's; main's engine allows it.
findings.check: A guard test: with OTHER another repository and BARE a local bare repository, `cd OTHER && git push BARE main && git push -f origin topic` is allowed, as `cd OTHER && git push -f origin topic` is.

evidence.command: Piped each line to `RAIL_CLOUD=0 <engine>/bin/rail hook guard` as a Bash PreToolUse event with cwd set to the ticket's worktree, first with main's engine, then this branch's; S/o1 is another git repository on main, S/o2 a bare repository.

runs.head: 467cc5dd82aa
runs.summary: No blocking or advisory findings; one parked guard gap that main has too. All six Done Contract checks pass, the vendored engine, pack, ruleset, workflow, template and AGENTS.md are identical to the framework at the `.rail/SOURCE` commit, and the framework's 161 tests pass at that commit. About 80 command lines piped through the guard on main's engine and this one differed only as intended, and a save fired mid-rebase commits nothing. findings.claim: A `cd DIR &&` is followed even when the shell skips it: in `true || cd OTHER_REPO && git push origin main` the shell never runs the cd, so the push to main (or `gh pr merge 5`) runs in this project, but the guard judges it as the other repository's and allows it. evidence.command: Piped each line to `RAIL_CLOUD=0 <engine>/bin/rail hook guard` as a Bash PreToolUse event with cwd set to the ticket's worktree, first with this branch's engine, then main's; OTHER is another git repository on branch main.
